sourceFiles: RainformerHWiv2/Drives/Drives.ini (UTF-16LE, 4384+ lines; 26 repeated per-drive-slot blocks A..Z + shared header/footer)
RainformerHWiv2/Drives/DriveMeasures.inc (plain ASCII despite folder convention, ~4700+ lines; 26 repeated per-drive-slot measure blocks + shared header)
RainformerHWiv2/@Resources/HWiNFO.inc (UTF-16LE; drive temp sensor table at lines ~153-256)
RainformerHWiv2/@Resources/Variables.inc (used to resolve alpha/opacity variables not given in the prompt's global summary)
RainformerHWiv2/@Resources/Styles.inc (UTF-16LE, 313 lines, read in full, resolves all MeterStyle chains used by this panel)
encodingNote: Drives.ini, DriveVars.inc, HWiNFO.inc, Styles.inc are UTF-16LE. DriveMeasures.inc is plain single-byte text (ASCII/UTF-8), inconsistent with its siblings but confirmed by byte inspection (first bytes 0x3B,0x5B = ';[' with no null interleave). Both decode correctly through the Read tool; ripgrep/Grep only works directly on DriveMeasures.inc, the UTF-16LE files needed PowerShell Get-Content -Encoding Unicode to locate section boundaries.

localVariables.scope: These are Drives.ini's own [Variables] block (layered on top of the shared @Resources/Variables.inc + DriveVars.inc + HWiNFO.inc includes).
localVariables.spaceInUseDrive_1_to_26: Per-drive toggle controlling whether the usage bar/text shows 'Used' (1) or 'Free' (0). Values in file: [1]=1 [2]=1 [3]=1 [4]=1 [5]=0 [6]=1 [7]=1 [8]=1 [9]=1 [10]=0 [11]=1 [12]=1 [13]=0 [14]=1 [15]=0 [16]=0 [17]=0 [18]=0 [19]=0 [20]=0 [21]=0 [22]=0 [23]=0 [24]=0 [25]=0 [26]=1. Toggled at runtime by clicking the invisible meterUsedFreeDriveN overlay (bang: SetVariable + WriteKeyValue back into DriveVars.inc, persisting the choice).
localVariables.note: These override/extend, they do not conflict with, the @Resources includes documented below.

resolvedColorsAndAlphas.note: Prompt's GLOBAL VARIABLES block already gave the RGB triples; the alpha/opacity components (needed for exact ARGB) were only in @Resources/Variables.inc and are filled in here.
resolvedColorsAndAlphas.note_ColorBarWarn: not previously listed; this is the bar 'low space / near full' warning color, alpha shared with colorBarAlpha=255
resolvedColorsAndAlphas.note_stroke: The background card's outline (Shape7 in StyleBackground) is stroked with StrokeColor/StrokeColorAlpha but at Stroke_Width=0, so it is effectively INVISIBLE in this (non-'recovery') theme. Do not render a visible border.

colorDrive_table_1_to_26.note: colorDriveN is the per-drive accent color, used (a) tinting the '(X:)' prefix of the drive label via InlineSetting/InlinePattern, and (b) as the LineColor of that drive's series in the shared write/read histogram graph.

geometry.note: All X/Y/W/H below (and throughout this document unless stated otherwise) are UNSCALED logical/design units taken directly from the .ini/.inc math, exactly as instructed. Every meter carries TransformationMatrix=#Scale#;0;0;#Scale#;#Scale#;#Scale#, i.e. the whole panel (including font rendering) is drawn at 1x logical layout then uniformly scaled 1.7x about the origin at render time. A D2D re-implementation should do the same: lay out in logical units, then apply a single 1.7x scale transform (do not scale coordinates by hand).
geometry.deg: literal file value is the string "[\x0x00B0]" (note the doubled 0x prefix -- appears to be a copy/paste artifact repeated skin-wide, also seen on the ElegantIcons glyph escapes like meterHideGraphs_'s Text=[\x0xe035]). Author's unambiguous intent is the degree sign U+00B0 (°). RECOMMENDATION: hardcode ° rather than trying to replicate Rainmeter's literal escape parsing.

backgroundShape.meterStyle: StyleBackground (@Resources/Styles.inc), applied by [MeterBackground] (Group=Background) at the very top of the panel, X=0 Y=0

overallSize.W_logical: (#BgShapeW#+0.06) + (#BgOffset#*2) = 196.06 + 10 = 206.06 (~= BgWidth, +0.06 fudge factor to avoid an antialiasing seam)
overallSize.H_logical: [MeterBackgroundHeight:Y] -- dynamic, equals the Y position of the invisible 1px anchor meter placed right after the two histogram graphs (see footerMeters); i.e. total content height = last-visible-drive-row-bottom + graph height (if shown) + BottomMargin + BgOffset + 2

twoZoneConstruction.shapes: Shape = RoundRect at (BgShapeX,BgShapeY)=(5,5), size (196,21), radius=CornerRadius(4), Fill=BgTopColor/BgTopOpacity, StrokeWidth=0. Shape2 = plain Rect at (5,13), size (196,14), no radius. Shape3 = Combine Shape | Union Shape2.
twoZoneConstruction.renders_as: Shape3 only (Shape and Shape2 are consumed by the Combine and are not drawn standalone, per Rainmeter Shape-meter semantics) -- net visual is a rounded-TOP-corners / square-bottom tab, ~22 logical units tall, filled BgTopColor(163,178,230) @ alpha 180.

twoZoneConstruction.shapes: Shape4 = RoundRect at (5, 24.5), size (196, [[CURRENTSECTION]:H] - ((BgShapeX+12.3)*2)), radius=CornerRadius(4), Fill=BgBodyColor/BgBodyOpacity. Shape5 = plain Rect at (5,24), size (196,15), no radius. Shape6 = Combine Shape4 | Union Shape5.
twoZoneConstruction.renders_as: Shape6 only -- net visual is a square-TOP / rounded-BOTTOM-corners body panel, height tracks total content height, filled BgBodyColor(230,230,230) @ alpha 180. Its square top overlaps/seams with the tab's square bottom so the two zones read as one continuous rounded card.

twoZoneConstruction.shapes: Shape7 = RoundRect at (4.5,4.5), size (197, totalH+Scale-2*BgShapeX), radius=(CornerRadius+0.5), StrokeWidth=(Stroke_Width*Scale)=0, StrokeColor/StrokeColorAlpha, Fill=0,0,0,0.
twoZoneConstruction.renders_as: Not visible in this theme (Stroke_Width=0 -> 0px stroke). Present in the file only; omit or render at 0 width.

hwinfoDriveTempSensors.note: Resolved from @Resources/HWiNFO.inc lines ~153-256. Rainmeter variable names are case-insensitive, so #HWiNFO-Drive3-Temp-SensorId# used in DriveMeasures.inc resolves to the value of HWiNFO-DRIVE3-Temp-SensorId defined here. All 26 drive slots share the SAME SensorId (0xf0000100); they are distinguished by SensorInstance (which physical drive controller port) and EntryId (which temperature entry within that instance). HWiNFOType=CurrentValue, HWiNFOLogHandler=0 for all.

5.EntryId: MISSING -- HWiNFO.inc defines HWiNFO-DRIVE5-Temp-SensorId and -SensorInstance but has NO -EntryId line at all (verified: line 171-173 jumps straight from SensorInstance=0x0 to the comment for Drive 6). #HWiNFO-Drive5-Temp-EntryId# will resolve to an empty/undefined variable. This is a genuine inconsistency in the source skin, not a transcription error -- flagged as a caveat.

table.10_to_26: SensorId=0xf0000100, SensorInstance=0x0, EntryId=0x0 for all (unused/placeholder slots)

howEnablementWorks: 1. Drives.ini/@Resources includes define up to 26 drive 'slots' (index 1..26, letter d1=A: .. d26=Z:), each with its own full set of measures+meters, almost all Hidden/Disabled by conditions.

2. @Resources/DriveVars.inc ShowDrives=ABCDEFGHIJKLMN is a string scanned letter-by-letter by [measureShowDrives] (Measure=String, IfMatch/IfMatch2..26). For each letter present, showDriveN is forced to 1 (persisted via WriteKeyValue back into DriveVars.inc); for letters absent (O-Z, plus any of A-N not in the string) showDriveN=0. This is the user-facing 'which drive letters do you want to show' master toggle -- separate strings ShowDrivesRWData / ShowDrivesOnGraph / ShowDrivesTemps (all also 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMN' in this file) independently gate the RW-rate row, the histogram-graph line, and the temperature display per drive.

3. [calcDriveNExists] (Measure=Calc) = (measureTotalDriveN > 0 && showDriveN==1) ? 1 : 0 -- i.e. a slot is 'real' only if Windows actually reports a total capacity > 0 for that drive letter (the drive is physically present/mounted) AND the user has not disabled it. The boolean result is written to the persistent variable existsDriveN (via WriteKeyValue into DriveVars.inc) and drives virtually every Hidden=/Disabled=/UpdateDivider= expression in the panel.

4. On THIS machine's snapshot (DriveVars.inc as shipped/cached): existsDrive1..2=0 (A:,B: absent), existsDrive3..9=1 (C:-I: present), existsDrive10..26=0. showDriveN=1 for slots 1-14, spaceInUseDriveN (used-vs-free display mode) = 1 for slots 1-4,6-9,11,12,14,26 and 0 for slots 5,10,13,15-25.
5. Net result: exactly 7 visible rows, for C,D,E,F,G,H,I, in that letter order (slot index order == alphabetical order since d{N} is a fixed A-Z map, not a sorted-by-presence remap).

criticalLayoutMechanism: This entire panel is one flat chain of 26 slots x 11 meters (286 meters) plus 26 slots x 15 measures (390 measures), almost all wrapped in Hidden=(...)/Disabled=(...) conditions keyed off existsDriveN. Rainmeter's documented behavior is that a Hidden meter contributes ZERO width/height to the R/r relative-position resolution of meters that come after it in file order -- this is the load-bearing trick that lets the flat 26-slot chain visually collapse to exactly the 7 populated rows (C..I) with no phantom gaps for A:,B:,J:..Z:. A D2D re-implementation should NOT attempt to replicate 286 always-present meters; it should simply iterate only the drives that exist (per activeDrives) and stack the 5 sub-rows below, using the row pitch rules below.

perDriveTemplate.placeholders: {N} = drive slot index 1..26 (only 3..9 populated on this machine). {d} = the drive-letter token #d{N}# (e.g. #d3# = 'C:'). All Y values below assume the drive at {N} is the CURRENT drive being laid out and that existsDrive{N}=1 (visible case); the collapsed/hidden-slot case is covered by criticalLayoutMechanism above.

measures.name: measureLabelDrive{N}
measures.details: Drive=#d{N}#, Label=1, IgnoreRemovable=0 (removable drives are NOT ignored/excluded). Returns the Windows volume label string (e.g. 'Local SSD') via %1.
measures.updateDivider: ((#existsDrive{N}#=0)?(-1):(1)) -- normal cadence when the drive is present, update-once-then-freeze when absent

measures.name: TempDrive{N}
measures.details: HWiNFOSensorId=#HWiNFO-Drive{N}-Temp-SensorId#, HWiNFOSensorInstance=#HWiNFO-Drive{N}-Temp-SensorInstance#, HWiNFOEntryId=#HWiNFO-Drive{N}-Temp-EntryId#, HWiNFOType=CurrentValue, HWiNFOLogHandler=0. Resolved sensor ids in hwinfoDriveTempSensors above.

measures.name: TempWarnDrive{N}
measures.note: The Calc measure's numeric output (-1..-5) is turned into an RGB-triple STRING by Substitute, then consumed directly as meterTempDrive{N}'s FontColor via the inline measure reference [TempWarnDrive{N}] (not a #Variable#) -- requires DynamicVariables=1 on the meter.

measures.name: measureUsedDrive{N}
measures.details: Drive=#d{N}#, InvertMeasure=1, IgnoreRemovable=0 -> returns USED bytes (FreeDiskSpace's native value is free space; InvertMeasure flips it to total-free=used).
measures.updateDivider: (((#existsDrive{N}#=0)||(#spaceInUseDrive{N}#=0))?(-1):(1)) -- only actively polled while the panel is in 'Used' display mode for this drive

ifConditions.ifFalseEffect: SetOption meterUsedBarDrive{N} BarColor #ColorBarWarn#,#colorBarAlpha# (220,20,60/255 -- near-full warning, >=75% used)

measures.name: measureFreeDrive{N}
measures.updateDivider: (((#existsDrive{N}#=0)||(#spaceInUseDrive{N}#=1))?(-1):(1)) -- only actively polled while in 'Free' display mode

measures.name: measureTotalDrive{N}
measures.details: Drive=#d{N}#, Total=1, IgnoreRemovable=0 -> total capacity bytes.
measures.note: Permanently Disabled=1 as a baseline; only refreshed via its OnChangeAction cascade: [!EnableMeasure calcDrive{N}Exists][!UpdateMeasure calcDrive{N}Exists][Delay 1000][!DisableMeasure calcDrive{N}Exists], and re-armed itself by measureShowDrives' IfMatchAction/IfNotMatchAction. This is a one-shot polling idiom for hot-plug/removable-drive detection; a D2D renderer can simply poll GetDiskFreeSpaceEx on its own schedule instead of replicating this exact enable/disable pulse chain.

ifConditions.ifTrueEffect: SetVariable existsDrive{N} 1, persist to DriveVars.inc, refresh Drive{N} measure/meter groups + Background
ifConditions.ifFalseEffect: SetVariable existsDrive{N} 0, persist, refresh same groups

measures.name: calcDrive{N}Graph
measures.details: No Formula key (defaults to 0); purely a vehicle for its IfCondition.

ifConditions.ifTrueEffect: Rebinds the shared histogram's series slot (index = 27-{N}, see graphMeters) to this drive's measures/color: SetOption meterWritingHistogram MeasureName{27-N} measureWritingDrive{N}; SetOption meterReadingHistogram MeasureName{27-N} measureReadingDrive{N}; both LineColor{27-N} set to #colorDrive{N}#,#colorHistogramAlpha#
ifConditions.ifFalseEffect: Rebinds that series slot to the neutral off-measure and 0-alpha color: MeasureName{27-N}=measureRWDriveOff, LineColor{27-N}=0,0,0,0 (flat, invisible line)

measures.name: measureSpaceInUseDrive{N}

ifConditions.ifTrueEffect: SetOption meterUsedFreeDrive{N}_ MeasureName measureFreeDrive{N}; Text 'Free: %1B' (Free display mode)
ifConditions.ifFalseEffect: SetOption meterUsedFreeDrive{N}_ MeasureName measureUsedDrive{N}; Text 'Used: %1B' (Used display mode, spaceInUseDrive{N}=1)

measures.note: This is how meterUsedFreeDrive{N}_ gets its MeasureName/Text at all -- the meter itself ships with MeasureName= blank in the .ini and is populated purely by this bang cascade at load/toggle time.

measures.name: measureWritingDrive{N}
measures.details: Category=LogicalDisk, Counter="Disk Write Bytes/sec", Name=#d{N}# (e.g. 'C:'). Raw bytes/sec.
measures.updateDivider: (((#existsDrive{N}#=0)||((#showDrive{N}RW#=0)&&(#showDrive{N}Graph#=0)))?(-1):(1)) -- polled if EITHER the RW-rate row OR the histogram graph needs it

measures.name: measureReadingDrive{N}
measures.details: Category=LogicalDisk, Counter="Disk Read Bytes/sec", Name=#d{N}#. Raw bytes/sec.

meters.name: meterLabelDrive{N}_
meters.styles: styleFirstLineText | StyleCenterAlign  [ONLY for slot N=1; ALL other slots (2..26, including every currently-visible C..I) use StyleCenterAlign | stylePrimaryText instead -- same resolved font/color, only the nominal Y-anchor documented in the unused style key differs; irrelevant because the meter's own explicit Y= always wins]

y.value: 32 for slot1 (absolute); otherwise prevMeterBottom+2 when this drive exists, prevMeterBottom+0 when it doesn't (prevMeter = the ReadingRateDrive of whatever slot immediately precedes this one in file order, which per criticalLayoutMechanism collapses through any intervening non-existent slots)

meters.h: auto (no explicit H; sized to one line of 8pt Trebuchet MS Bold text -- font-metric dependent, must be measured by the D2D text layout, not hardcoded)
meters.fontColor: #colorText#,#colorTextAlpha# = 0,0,0/205 for the body of the string
meters.text: (#d{N}#) %1  where %1 = measureLabelDrive{N} (the volume label, e.g. 'Local SSD')
meters.inlineOverride: InlineSetting=Color|#colorDrive{N}#,#colorHistogramAlpha# with InlinePattern=^(.*\)).*  -- recolors just the '(X:)' prefix (through the first ')') using this drive's accent color at alpha 250; the rest of the label text stays default colorText/205.

meters.name: meterTempDrive{N}

y.value: same row as the label (0r) when the temp is shown; +13 if the drive exists but temp display is toggled off (still Hidden, so purely a bookkeeping offset); +0 if the drive doesn't exist

meters.fontColor: [TempWarnDrive{N}] -- live inline measure reference, resolves to one of the 5 DevTempWarnColorTh strings

meters.name: meterUsedFreeDrive{N}_

y.value: prevBottom(label/temp row)+0 when exists (RowSpacing-1=0), i.e. flush new row directly under the label/temp row; +0 (no-op) when absent

meters.fontColor: #colorText#,#colorTextAlpha# (0,0,0/205); briefly turns #colorActiveTitle#,#colorActiveTitleAlpha# (255,128,0/255) on mouse-hover via the invisible overlay meter, see skipped[]
meters.text: Set at runtime by measureSpaceInUseDrive{N}'s IfCondition, NOT present as a static Text= key: either 'Used: %1B' (measureUsedDrive{N}) or 'Free: %1B' (measureFreeDrive{N}), matching this drive's spaceInUseDrive{N} toggle.
meters.autoScaleUnits: Rainmeter AutoScale on a byte count: scales by 1024 through k/M/G/T, %1 substitutes as '<value> <prefix-letter>' (e.g. '1.1 T'), the literal 'B' in the Text template completes it to 'TB'.

y.value: same row as meterUsedFreeDrive{N}_ (Used/Free left, Total right, one visual row -- this is the literal source of the panel's 'Used: 1.1TB ... Total: 1.9TB' line; there is no combined X/Y string, it is two separately-aligned meters)

meters.name: meterUsedBarDrive{N}
meters.barColor: set dynamically by measureUsedPercentDrive{N}'s IfCondition: #colorBar#,#colorBarAlpha# (93,141,172/255) if used% < 75, else #ColorBarWarn#,#colorBarAlpha# (220,20,60/255)

meters.name: meterFreeBarDrive{N}

y.expr: r (no explicit Y; inherits same-Y-as-previous-meter from StyleLeftAlign_r, i.e. identical slot to meterUsedBarDrive{N})

meters.barColor: set dynamically by measureFreePercentDrive{N}'s IfCondition: colorBar if free% > 25, else ColorBarWarn
meters.notes: Flip=1 fills the bar right-to-left using the FREE percentage, which visually reconstructs the same 'used portion filled from the left' look as the Used-mode bar even though a different measure/direction drives it -- exactly one of UsedBar/FreeBar renders at a time, occupying the identical rectangle.

meters.name: meterFixEmptyBarDrive{N}
meters.notes: Dead/vestigial meter -- never renders under any condition observed in the file. Safe to omit entirely in a re-implementation.

meters.name: meterWritingIndicatorDrive{N}
meters.text: down-arrow glyph, file literal '[\x0x37]' (see notes on the doubled-0x escape quirk; intended glyph is ElegantIcons codepoint 0x37, a downward arrow used here to denote 'writing')
meters.fontColor: starts #colorInactiveButton#,#colorInactiveButtonAlpha# (120,120,120/255); set to #colorRed#,#colorRedAlpha# (204,0,0/255) by measureWritingDrive{N}Calc whenever write throughput > 0

meters.name: meterReadingIndicatorDrive{N}
meters.text: up-arrow glyph, file literal '[\x0x36]' (ElegantIcons codepoint 0x36, upward arrow, denotes 'reading')
meters.fontColor: same idle/active red logic as the write arrow, driven by measureReadingDrive{N}Calc

meters.name: meterWritingRateDrive{N}

y.expr: ((#existsDrive{N}#=1) ? 2 : 0) r  (both ternary branches literally evaluate to 2 in the source -- the showDrive{N}RW check inside the ternary is a no-op, always yields 2)
y.value: prevMeterY(reading-arrow row)+2 -- NOT bottom-relative, so this sits inside/near the bottom edge of the 14px-tall arrow row rather than fully below it (compact/overlapping-by-design layout)

meters.fontColor: #colorText2#,#colorText2Alpha# = 60,65,62/205 (does NOT change color with activity -- only the arrow glyph above does)
meters.numOfDecimals: NOT explicitly set on this meter (no NumOfDecimals key) -- relies on Rainmeter's built-in default, which differs from the explicit NumOfDecimals=1 used on the Used/Free/Total text meters. See notes[] caveat re: the example '20.6 M' given in the task prompt.
meters.note_units: Text is bare '%1' with no trailing literal unit letter, so AutoScale's own SI-prefix output (e.g. '20.6 M') is the ENTIRE displayed string -- unlike Total/Used which append a literal 'B'.

meters.name: meterReadingRateDrive{N}

y.expr: r (from StyleRightAlign_r, overriding styleSecondaryText's own RowSpacing-R default) -> same row as meterWritingRateDrive{N}

meters.numOfDecimals: not explicit, same caveat as meterWritingRateDrive{N}
meters.note: This is the LAST meter in each drive's 11-meter file-order block; the next drive slot's meterLabelDrive{N+k}_ chains its Y off of THIS meter's bottom (Y + H=10), which per criticalLayoutMechanism lands exactly 2 logical units below wherever the arrow row visually ends, giving the observed clean stacking between consecutive visible drives.

perDriveTemplate.rowPitch: Within one visible drive block, 5 sub-rows stack with ZERO gap between each other's bottom edges (all inter-row offsets resolve to RowSpacing-1=0): [row1: label(center)+temp(right)] -> [row2: used/free(left)+total(right)] -> [row3: usage bar, full width] -> [row4: write-arrow(left)+read-arrow(right), H=14] -> [row5: write-rate(left)+read-rate(right), offset +2 from row4's TOP (not bottom), effectively nested near the bottom of the 14px arrow row]. Between consecutive VISIBLE drive blocks, the gap is a flat +2 logical units (RowSpacing+1) applied on top of the previous visible block's row5 bottom (row5.Y + row5.H = row4.Y+2+10 = row4.Y+12, then +2 = row4.Y+14, i.e. exactly where the 14px arrow row would have ended -- a deliberately tuned coincidence). Two of the five sub-row heights (row1, row2) have no explicit H in the .ini and are auto-sized to one line of 8pt Trebuchet MS text; a pixel-exact D2D re-implementation must measure that text height (at 1x logical scale, Bold for row1/label, Bold for row2, then multiply the whole assembly by Scale=1.7) rather than assume a fixed constant.

perDriveDifferences.C: slot 3, first VISIBLE row (immediately after the title zone at Y=TopMarginFormula=32, since slots 1 and 2 (A:,B:) are non-existent and contribute zero height). Used-mode bar/text. Accent color 255,97,0 (orange). Histogram series 24.
perDriveDifferences.D: slot 4, Used-mode. Accent 217,0,252 (magenta). Histogram series 23. Immediately follows C with the standard +2 gap.
perDriveDifferences.E: slot 5, FREE-mode (spaceInUseDrive5=0) -- this is the only one of the 7 active drives whose row2/row3 show 'Free: xxx' and a right-filling free-percentage bar instead of 'Used: xxx'. Accent 127,147,146 (grey-teal). Histogram series 22. Its HWiNFO EntryId is missing from HWiNFO.inc (see hwinfoDriveTempSensors) -- a genuine source-file gap, flag for QA on the real machine's temperature reading.
perDriveDifferences.G: slot 7, Used-mode. Accent 0,159,255 (sky blue). Histogram series 20.
perDriveDifferences.I: slot 9, Used-mode, LAST visible row (slots 10-26 all non-existent, contribute zero height before the shared histogram graphs begin). Accent 121,182,62 (olive green). Histogram series 18.
perDriveDifferences.generalNote: Beyond the above (display mode, accent color, sensor instance id, histogram series slot, and the one missing EntryId), the 7 active drives are laid out and behave 100% identically -- same fonts, sizes, alignment rules, thresholds, and row pitch.

graphMeters.note: IMPORTANT correction to the initial framing: there is NOT a separate small graph/bar per drive row. There are exactly two shared, panel-wide multi-series Line meters below the whole 26-slot drive list -- one for write throughput, one for read throughput -- each containing 26 fixed series (one dedicated series slot per possible drive letter, NOT compacted/reflowed for only-7-active-drives). Per-drive activity is expressed ONLY as: (a) the write/read arrow glyph color flip in row4, (b) the rate text in row5, and (c) that drive's own fixed-position line inside these two shared graphs.

meterWritingHistogram.style: StyleHalfLengthGraphLeft (X=ContentMarginFormula+0=7, W=(ContentWidth-2)/2=94, H=25, GraphStart=Left, Autoscale=#GraphAutoscale#=0, SolidColor=EmptyBarColor/EmptyBarColorAlpha as the background track)

y.value: prevBottom(the last, possibly-collapsed, drive meter i.e. the final slot 26 ReadingRateDrive26)+4 when ShowGraph=1, else +0 (whole graph collapses to zero height when the user has toggled graphs off via meterHideGraphs_)

meterWritingHistogram.seriesMapping: MeasureName{k} / LineColor{k} for k=1..26 (k=1 has no numeric suffix) are wired to drive slot (27-k): series1=Drive26 ... series24=Drive3(C) ... series23=Drive4(D) ... series22=Drive5(E) ... series21=Drive6(F) ... series20=Drive7(G) ... series19=Drive8(H) ... series18=Drive9(I) ... series26=Drive1. This 27-k mapping is FIXED at file-load and then each calcDrive{N}Graph measure re-points its OWN dedicated series (not a shared/reflowing pool) between the real measure+color (drive exists & graphed) or the neutral measureRWDriveOff + fully-transparent 0,0,0,0 color (drive absent or graphing disabled for it).

meterReadingHistogram.style: StyleHalfLengthGraphRight (Y=r i.e. same row as the writing histogram, W=94, H=25, GraphStart=Right)

x.value: immediately to the right of meterWritingHistogram (its X+W) plus a 2-unit gap -- together the two halves form one continuous full-width (188-ish) graph area split write-left/read-right

meterReadingHistogram.seriesMapping: identical 27-k mapping, mirrored for read measures/colors

graphMeters.measureRWDriveOff: Measure=Calc, Formula=0, Disabled=1 -- the shared 'off' placeholder measure bound to any series slot whose drive is absent or not graphed; always reads 0 and is paired with a fully transparent LineColor so it draws nothing.

headerMeters.name: MeterBackground
headerMeters.note: Group=Background, MeterStyle=StyleBackground, see backgroundShape above. First meter in the file, anchors the whole panel at (0,0).

headerMeters.name: meterTitle
headerMeters.stringCase: None (overrides styleTitle's UPPER, but 'DRIVES' is already upper-case so no visible difference)
headerMeters.hoverBehavior: MouseOverAction on the invisible meterTitleClickableRegion overlay changes this text to 'This PC' in colorActiveTitle (255,128,0) and opens the This-PC shell folder on click; MouseLeaveAction reverts to 'DRIVES' in default color.

headerMeters.name: ControlSettings_ / meterHideGraphs_ / meterShowGraphs_
headerMeters.note: Top-right icon row (gear/settings glyph + collapse/expand-graph toggle glyphs), font ElegantIcons, colorInactiveButton. Purely chrome/interaction, no drive data. See 'skipped'.

footerMeters.name: MeterBackgroundHeight
footerMeters.details: 1x1, fully transparent (SolidColor=255,255,255,0), X=0, Y=(#BottomMargin#+#BgOffset#+2) R off of the reading histogram (i.e. total content bottom + 3 + 5 + 2 = +10 past the graphs), W=(BgWidth*Scale), H=1.
footerMeters.purpose: Pure measurement anchor: StyleBackground's Shape/Shape4/Shape7 all reference [MeterBackgroundHeight:Y] to know the total logical height of the card so the rounded-rect background can stretch to fit however many drives + whether the graph is shown. A D2D re-implementation replaces this with a simple 'compute total content height, then draw the background rect at that height' step -- no need for a literal anchor meter.

skipped: ControlSettings_, meterHideGraphs_, meterShowGraphs_ (top-right chrome icons: settings gear, collapse/expand-graph toggle) -- Group=Controls/hideGraph/showGraph, purely interactive, no per-drive data.

ControlSettings, meterHideGraphs, meterShowGraphs (no trailing underscore) -- invisible Meter=Image StyleMouseRegion|StyleMouseRegionStringButtonHover overlays sized/positioned FROM the visible '_'-suffixed meters via [meter_:X]/[meter_:Y]/[meter_:W]/[meter_:H] measure-references, purely to catch mouse clicks/hover and drive the *_ meters' hover color-swap and the show/hide-graph bang commands. Zero visual footprint of their own (SolidColor=255,255,255,0 or 0,0,0,0).
meterTitleClickableRegion -- invisible overlay over part of the title, opens 'This PC' (CLSID {20D04FE0-3AEA-1069-A2D8-08002B30309D}) on click and swaps the title text/color on hover.

meterLabelDrive{N} and meterUsedFreeDrive{N} (no trailing underscore, appear ONCE at the very end of Drives.ini for N=1..26, Group=DriveMr) -- invisible Meter=Image, SolidColor=0,0,0,0 hit-test overlays sized from their '_'-suffixed visible counterparts. meterLabelDrive{N}'s LeftMouseUpAction=[#d{N}#] opens that drive letter in Explorer and its hover actions swap the visible label's text to 'OPEN'/back. meterUsedFreeDrive{N}'s LeftMouseUpAction toggles spaceInUseDrive{N} (flips Used<->Free display mode) and its hover actions swap the visible Used/Free text's color to colorActiveTitle/back. Neither renders any pixels itself.

MeasureSettingsScript (Measure=Script running Settings.lua) and measureShowDrives / measureShowDrivesRWData / measureShowDrivesOnGraph / measureShowDrivesTemps (the 4 big letter-scanning String measures in DriveMeasures.inc that translate the ShowDrives*/ShowDrivesRWData*/etc strings into the 26 per-slot showDriveN/showDriveNRW/showDriveNGraph/showDriveNTemp booleans) -- these are configuration/settings-UI plumbing (also referenced by a Settings*.ini not requested here), not part of the rendered data panel itself. Their RESULT (the resolved per-drive booleans) is already captured in activeDrives/perDriveDifferences.
verticalFlowSummary: Panel origin (0,0), unscaled/logical units, whole assembly later uniformly scaled by 1.7: [1] StyleBackground rounded-card shape drawn first (its final height is computed retroactively from everything below, via the MeterBackgroundHeight anchor). [2] Title 'DRIVES' centered at Y=9, plus top-right settings/collapse-graph icon chrome (non-data). [3] Drive list begins at Y=TopMarginFormula(32): for each of the up-to-26 drive-letter slots in fixed alphabetical order, IF that slot's existsDriveN=1 it renders a 5-sub-row block (label+temp / used-or-free+total / usage-bar / write-arrow+read-arrow / write-rate+read-rate text) stacked with 0px internal gaps and a +2 logical-unit gap before the next EXISTING slot's block; non-existent slots are fully present in the file/measure graph but Hidden and, per Rainmeter's documented Hidden-meter-has-zero-size-for-relative-positioning behavior, contribute no vertical space, so the visible list reads as a tight, gapless stack of only the present drives. On this machine that is exactly 7 rows: C, D, E, F, G, H, I (in that fixed letter order, not sorted by any other criterion). [4] Immediately below the (possibly fully-collapsed) 26th slot, IF ShowGraph=1, two half-width Line-graph meters render side by side (write-history left, read-history right), each a FIXED 26-series multi-line chart where each of the 26 possible drives owns one permanently-assigned series slot (index 27-N) that is either colored+fed real data (drive exists & graphed) or fully transparent+fed a constant 0 (drive absent/not graphed) -- this is the panel's only graph, shared across all drives, not per-row. [5] A final 1px invisible anchor meter records the total content height for the background shape to size itself against, then (out of scope for static rendering) the interactive click/hover overlay meters are layered on top.
notes: The prompt's illustrative numbers ('52°C', '1.1 TB / 1.9 TB', '20.6 M') are visually consistent with, but not literal reproductions of, the actual Text templates: temperature really is '%1#deg##TempUnitLetter#'; Used/Total really are two SEPARATE left- and right-aligned meters on one row reading 'Used: <auto>B' ... 'Total: <auto>B' (no literal '/'); and the R/W rate meters really do use bare '%1' AutoScale output with NO trailing 'B' (so 'M' alone, not 'MB'), matching the given '20.6 M' example.

CAVEAT -- NumOfDecimals: measureTotalDrive{N}/meterUsedFreeDrive{N}_ explicitly set NumOfDecimals=1 (so 'Total: 1.9TB' truly has one decimal). meterWritingRateDrive{N}/meterReadingRateDrive{N} do NOT set NumOfDecimals at all and rely on Rainmeter's own default for AutoScale (commonly documented as 0 decimals) -- if the real skin visually shows a decimal on rate text (as the prompt's '20.6 M' example implies), verify Rainmeter's actual runtime default/behavior before hardcoding 0 vs 1 decimal place for the write/read rate numbers; this could not be settled from the static file alone.

CAVEAT -- HWiNFO-Drive5-Temp-EntryId is entirely absent from @Resources/HWiNFO.inc (verified by direct read of lines 170-173); drive E's temperature plugin measure will receive an empty/undefined HWiNFOEntryId. Flag for the real machine / do not silently default this to 0x0 or 0x1000000 without checking actual behavior.

CAVEAT -- Several Text/glyph values use a literal doubled escape prefix '\x0xHHHH' (e.g. #deg#, the write/read arrow glyphs, the settings-gear glyph) instead of the more usual single '\xHHHH'. This is consistent skin-wide (not a one-off typo isolated to Drives), so it is very likely intentional/tolerated by Rainmeter's parser, but its exact resolved character could not be verified without running the live engine. Recommended treatment for re-implementation: use the obviously-intended Unicode/PUA codepoint directly (° for #deg#, ElegantIcons 0x37/0x36 for the arrows) rather than reproducing the literal escape text.

DriveMeasures.inc is plain ASCII/UTF-8 while every other file read for this task (Drives.ini, DriveVars.inc, HWiNFO.inc, Styles.inc, Variables.inc) is UTF-16LE -- purely a file-encoding curiosity, does not affect resolved values, but affected which tool (Grep vs PowerShell Get-Content) could locate section boundaries during extraction.

The background outline (Shape7 in StyleBackground) is defined with a real StrokeColor/StrokeColorAlpha but Stroke_Width=0, so it is invisible in the (default/non-'recovery') theme actually in use here -- do not render a visible card border.

This document intentionally generalizes the per-drive MEASURES/METERS as an {N}-templated pattern (verified identical, section-by-section, for slot 1, 2, 3, 4 explicitly and spot-checked structurally consistent through slot 17 via the section-header scan) rather than transcribing all 26 x (15 measures + 11 meters) = 676 sections verbatim; perDriveDifferences + activeDrives.perDriveResolvedState give every value that actually differs across the 7 currently-active drives (C-I).
